title: Fluid Statics & Surface Tension — MCQs
description: Conceptual questions and short numerical checks covering Archimedes' principle, Pascal's law, buoyancy, law of floatation, surface tension, surface energy, contact angle and capillarity.

questions.q: State Archimedes' principle. What does it imply for a body immersed in a fluid?
options: An immersed body experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the displaced fluid
Pressure in a fluid increases with depth
Buoyant force equals weight of object
questions.explanation: Archimedes' principle: A body wholly or partially immersed in a fluid experiences an upthrust equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.

questions.q: Pascal's law states that a change in pressure applied to an enclosed fluid is transmitted undiminished. Which device uses this principle?
questions.explanation: A hydraulic press multiplies force by transmitting pressure through an enclosed fluid according to Pascal's law.

questions.q: If an object buoyant force equals its weight, the object will:
questions.explanation: If buoyant force = weight, net force is zero and object floats (neutrally stable at that level) or remains suspended.

questions.q: Up-thrust is:
options: The downward force due to gravity
The upward force exerted by a fluid on an immersed body
questions.explanation: Up-thrust (buoyant force) is the net upward force exerted by a fluid on a submerged or partially submerged body.

questions.q: Fluid pressure at a depth depends on:
options: Depth and fluid density and gravity
questions.explanation: Pressure p = ρgh (plus atmospheric pressure). It depends on fluid density ρ, gravitational acceleration g and depth h.

questions.q: Center of buoyancy is:
options: Centre of mass of the body
questions.explanation: Center of buoyancy is the centroid of the displaced fluid volume and is the point where buoyant force effectively acts.

questions.q: Metacentre relates to stability of floating bodies. A body is stable if the metacentre (M) is:
questions.explanation: For stability, M must lie above G (metacentric height GM positive). Then restoring moment returns the body to equilibrium.

questions.q: The law of floatation states:
options: A floating body displaces its own weight of the fluid
A floating body displaces volume equal to its own volume
Buoyant force equals volume of body
Floating does not depend on density
questions.explanation: Law of floatation: A floating body displaces a weight of fluid equal to its own weight.

questions.q: A wooden block (density 600 kg/m³) floats on water (ρ = 1000 kg/m³). Fraction submerged is:
questions.explanation: Fraction submerged = density_block / density_fluid = 600/1000 = 0.6.

questions.q: A metal piece of mass 2 kg floats because of some trapped air; the weight of displaced water is 2g N. This statement demonstrates:
questions.explanation: Floating implies displaced fluid weight = weight of object (Archimedes).

questions.q: Surface tension arises because:
options: Fluid molecules at surface have fewer neighbors and net inward attraction
Surface molecules have more kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Surface molecules experience unbalanced cohesive forces leading to an effective 'skin' which minimizes surface area — surface tension.

questions.q: Which of these demonstrates surface tension?
options: A needle floating on water despite being denser than water
questions.explanation: A carefully placed needle can float due to surface tension producing upward force along the contact perimeter.

questions.q: Surface tension has SI units:
questions.explanation: Surface tension γ is force per unit length (N/m) — equivalently energy per unit area (J/m²).

questions.q: Relation between surface energy (E) and surface tension (γ) for area ΔA is:
questions.explanation: Surface tension equals surface energy per unit area: ΔE = γ ΔA (increase in surface energy when area increases by ΔA).

questions.q: If surface area of a liquid film increases by 0.02 m² and γ = 0.072 N/m, the increase in surface energy is:
questions.explanation: ΔE = γΔA = 0.072 × 0.02 = 0.00144 J (note: ensure calculation units). Correction: 0.072×0.02 = 0.00144 J (so option '0.00144 J' is the right numeric). (Select the numeric equivalent.)

questions.q: Angle of contact (θ) is defined between:
options: Tangent to liquid surface and tangent to solid at contact measured in liquid
questions.explanation: Angle of contact is the angle between the tangent to the liquid surface and the solid surface measured inside the liquid.

questions.q: If a liquid wets a solid, the contact angle θ is:
questions.explanation: Wettting implies θ < 90° (e.g., water on clean glass). If θ > 90°, liquid does not wet the surface.

questions.q: Capillarity (capillary action) is best explained as:
options: Movement of liquid in narrow tube due to surface tension and contact angle
questions.explanation: Capillary rise or fall happens due to surface tension and the contact angle between liquid and tube material.

questions.q: Capillary rise height h in a tube of radius r is given by:
questions.explanation: Standard formula: h = (2γ cosθ)/(ρ g r).

questions.q: Water rises in a glass capillary of radius 0.5 mm by 30 mm. Taking γ = 0.072 N/m and ρ = 1000 kg/m³, estimate contact angle (approx). (Use g = 9.8 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Using h = 2γ cosθ/(ρ g r). For given numbers cosθ ≈ hρ g r /(2γ) → substituting gives cosθ ≈ (0.03×1000×9.8×0.0005)/(2×0.072) ≈ close to 1 so θ ≈ 0° (nearly complete wetting).

questions.q: A cube of side 0.1 m and density 600 kg/m³ is placed gently on water. Its upthrust is approximately (take g = 9.8):
questions.explanation: Volume displaced when floating = V_sub = (ρ_obj/ρ_water) V_total. Weight = mass×g = ρ_obj V_total g = 600×0.001×9.8 = 5.88 N. Upthrust equals weight = 5.88 N.

questions.q: A floating body displaces 0.02 m³ of fluid of density 1000 kg/m³. The buoyant force is:
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = weight of displaced fluid = ρ V g = 1000×0.02×9.8 = 196 N. (If option 19.6 exists, verify units — correct numeric is 196 N.)

questions.q: A lead piece (density 11340 kg/m³) attached to a block of wood sinks it. Which factor directly reduces the effective weight the block experiences in water?
questions.explanation: Upthrust (buoyancy) reduces the apparent weight of immersed bodies.

questions.q: A hydraulic lift has small piston area 0.01 m² and large piston area 1.0 m². If 200 N is applied on small piston ignoring losses, ideal upward force on large piston is:
questions.explanation: Pressure p = F/A_small = 200/0.01 = 20000 Pa. On large piston F = p A_large = 20000×1.0 = 20000 N (idealized).

questions.q: Which expression correctly gives work done to increase a liquid surface area by ΔA with surface tension γ?
questions.explanation: Work required to create new surface area ΔA is W = γ ΔA (surface energy increase).

questions.q: Why does a soap film have two surfaces affecting surface energy?
options: Film has two liquid–air interfaces (front & back) so energy is 2γA
questions.explanation: A thin film has two interfaces — both contribute surface energy; total energy change is 2γΔA.

questions.q: Which liquid will have largest capillary rise in the same glass tube: water (γ ≈ 0.072 N/m), mercury (γ ≈ 0.485 N/m), or ethanol (γ ≈ 0.022 N/m)? Assume contact angle for water nearly 0°, mercury >90°.
questions.explanation: Although mercury has larger γ, it does not wet glass (cosθ negative) causing depression. Water (wetting) gives significant positive rise; ethanol has smaller γ but also wets — water typically gives a larger rise here.

questions.q: A ship loaded high has G (centre of gravity) raised. This affects stability by:
questions.explanation: Raising G reduces GM = BM - BG typically making the ship less stable (smaller righting moment).

questions.q: If an object is completely submerged and released, it will rise if:
options: Its centre of gravity is high
questions.explanation: If object density < fluid density, net buoyant force exceeds weight and it rises.

questions.q: A capillary tube of radius 1×10⁻⁴ m has water rise 0.076 m at 20°C. Using ρ = 1000 kg/m³ and g = 9.8 m/s², estimate γ cosθ ≈
questions.explanation: From h = 2γ cosθ/(ρ g r) ⇒ γ cosθ = (ρ g r h)/2 = (1000×9.8×1e-4×0.076)/2 ≈ 0.0371 N/m. (Nearest listed: 0.072 is typical γ for water but computed value depends on rounding and contact angle; the idea: γcosθ order 10^-2 N/m.)
